rows.answer: Section 4 imposes income tax on the taxable income of every person who has taxable income for the tax year, i.e., on the taxable income of each taxpayer. The tax is levied at the rate or rates specified in Division I or Division II of Part I of the First Schedule, as applicable to the taxpayer, for tax year 2027 onward.[1]

rows.answer: Under section 15, “rent” means any amount received or receivable by the owner of land or a building as consideration for the use or occupation of, or the right to use or occupy, that land or building, and it also includes any forfeited deposit paid under a contract for the sale of land or a building [1]. The definition is reiterated in the definitions section of the Ordinance, which states that “rent” means rent as defined in sub‑section (2) of section 15 and includes an amount treated as rent under section 16 [2]. Additionally, any amount included in rent for the provision of amenities, utilities or other services connected with the renting of the building is also chargeable to tax, though under the head “Income from Other Sources” [1].

rows.answer: Under the Income Tax Ordinance, a "tax year" is a twelve‑month period ending on 30 June and is normally identified by the calendar year in which that date falls (the “normal tax year”) [1]. A person may be permitted to use a different twelve‑month period as a “special tax year” if the Commissioner approves an application, and such special year is also denoted by the calendar year in which its closing date falls [1]. The definition of “tax year” in the Ordinance’s definitions section refers back to this provision in section 74 [3].

rows.answer: An individual must be present in Pakistan for at least one hundred and eighty‑three days in aggregate during the tax year to be deemed a resident individual [1]. For this purpose, any part of a day in which the individual is present (including arrival and departure days) is counted as a full day, except days spent in transit, as per Rule 14 of the Income Tax Rules [2].

rows.answer: For tax year 2027 the foreign tax credit on foreign‑source income is limited to the lesser of (a) the foreign income tax actually paid (including foreign withholding tax) or (b) the Pakistan tax that would be payable on that income, which is calculated by applying the taxpayer’s average Pakistan tax rate for the year to the net foreign‑source income. The credit is applied head‑by‑head and cannot exceed the Pakistan tax liability on that head of income.

rows.answer: If you cannot explain the nature and source of an investment, money, valuable article or the funds used for an expenditure, the amount will be deemed unexplained and must be included in your taxable income. The unexplained amount is added to income from Other Sources, or if it relates to suppressed production, sales or receipts, to income from Business, in the tax year to which it relates if the asset is situated in Pakistan or is Pakistan‑source, or in the preceding tax year if it is foreign‑source and discovered later [1]. The Commissioner may also include any shortfall between the declared cost and a reasonable cost of the investment or expenditure as income from Other Sources [2]. An exception applies where foreign exchange up to Rs 5 million is remitted through normal banking channels and a bank certificate is produced; such amounts are not subject to the provisions of section 111 [2].
